subject.title: Embedded agent: auto-rotate (or persist a marker) on context-overflow give_up instead of wedging the session until manual /reset

question: Should exhausted embedded-agent context-overflow recovery persist a durable blocked-overflow state, auto-rotate and replay the pending turn once, or keep manual recovery with better visibility?
rationale: The current code and docs intentionally preserve the session mapping after failed overflow recovery, while the requested change chooses new core session recovery and durable state semantics for autonomous agents.

options.title: Persist blocked state first
options.body: Add a durable overflow-blocked marker plus operator-visible recovery affordance without silently replaying the pending turn on a new session.

options.title: Guarded one-shot rotation
options.body: Rotate and replay once only after compaction and truncation are exhausted, with replay-safety gates and a per-session loop cap.

options.title: Keep manual recovery
options.body: Keep the documented `/reset` or `/new` contract and improve only logs, diagnostics, docs, or UI visibility.

recommendation.title: Persist blocked state first
recommendation.body: Add a durable overflow-blocked marker plus operator-visible recovery affordance without silently replaying the pending turn on a new session.

likelyOwner.reason: Session-store policy and cross-surface recovery semantics are the central decision, and steipete has the strongest sampled history on that surface.
